blocks.content: A Dockerfile is a plain text file containing, step by step, the exact instructions needed to build a Docker image. It is the recipe, docker build is the act of cooking it.

A Dockerfile reads top to bottom, each line an instruction (FROM, RUN, COPY, and the rest covered throughout this module) that Docker executes in sequence, building up the final image one layer at a time.

blocks.alt: A plain text recipe, turned into an image

blocks.content:
FROM node:18
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json .
RUN npm install
COPY . .
CMD ["node", "index.js"]

blocks.content: Unlike a manually configured server, a Dockerfile is not tribal knowledge locked in someone's head, it is a readable, version-controllable description of exactly how the environment is assembled, that produces the identical result every single time it is built.

blocks.alt: A readable recipe that reproduces exactly, every time

blocks.content: A Dockerfile is almost always committed to the same git repository as the application it packages, right alongside the source code. This means the exact steps to build a working environment travel with the code itself, reviewable in the same pull requests as everything else.

blocks.alt: Version-controlled alongside the code it packages

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A Dockerfile is a plain text, ordered list of build instructions, the readable recipe that docker build turns into an image.
Because it is just a text file, it lives in version control with your code, fully reviewable and reproducible.
